To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high carbohydrate diet increases rates of glucose metabolism in adipose cells of obese but not of insulin-deficient diabetic animals.
the high carbohydrate diet increased insulin secretion in the spontaneously obese rats, whereas in the streptozotcin-induced diabetic rats the diet failed to increase insulin output.

the high-carbohydrate diet leads to increased glucose transport, oxidation and lipogenesis in adipocytes of spontaneously obese rats, but not in adipocytes of insulin-deficient diabetic animals, and that the increased rates of glucose metabolism in the obese animals most probably are due to the increased insulin secretion induced by the diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a high carbohydrate, low protein diet on glucose transport and metabolism in adipose tissue.
the effects of a high carbohydrate intake on adipocyte glucose transport and metabolism in obese and diabetic rats.
the effects of diet on glucose metabolism in spontaneously diabetic rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a high carbohydrate diet can lead to increased rates of adipocyte metabolism in spontaneously obese but not in insulin-deficient diabetic animals.
a high carbohydrate diet in the presence of hyperinsulinemia increases the rate of glucose transport, glucose metabolism, and fat synthesis in adipose tissue.
in the obese animal, the diet induced relative hyperinsulinism, which led to an increase of glucose metabolism in adipose tissue, whereas the diabetic rats did not respond to the diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in obese animals a high carbohydrate diet is beneficial, but in insulin-deficient diabetic animals the diet has no beneficial effect on glucose metabolism in adipose tissue.

in the obese rat, the increased insulin secretion induced by a high carbohydrate diet is the most important stimulus for the increased rates of glucose transport and glucose metabolism in adipose tissue.
a diet-induced relative hyper-insulinemia leads to increased rates of glucose transport and glucose metabolism in adipose tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diet-induced relative insulinemia is the main mediator of the diet-induced changes in glucose metabolism.
a high carbohydrate diet can lead to augmented cellular glucose transport and glucose metabolism, provided that the animal can respond with increased insulin secretion.
the effects of a high carbohydrate intake are mediated by changes in insulin secretion.
